It's actually going pretty good. I fixed this problem I had with one of our backup web servers. Grub was completely borked up. It turned out that the issue was because of the software raid lost two drives. It was a RAID 5 with a hot spare, so it was still running, but for some reason, grub got hosed and no matter what I did to fix it, it wouldn't work. I didn't even think of looking at the drives. On a whim I checked out mdstat and saw that only 4 drives were active. So, I replaced the drives and added them back to the raid, waiting a day for the rebuild and now everything works as expected.

I didn't even think about it because I wasn't the one who set the server up. Someone else did, placed it on my lap and said "here, it's your problem now." I wouldn't have done a software raid, especially on a backup web server. If that machine has the potential to become live, I would never risk it on software raid.
